lead.headline: 438 place names still say "Negro"; in 2020-23, 641 "Squaw" names changed vs at least 41 "Negro" or n-word ones
lead.number: 438 official federal names in the English sense (426 current, 12 historical); 105 list the n-word as an older name in the same file
lead.watch_out: Citation dates stop on 2023-03-17, so renamings after that can't be counted by year; 50 Spanish "negro" (black) names were removed by hand.

sources.quote: Today, 469 pieces of geography still contain the replacement word in their name, according to the geographic names database managed by the U.S. Geological Survey.
At least 558 place names across the nation include derogatory words referring to African Americans, Vocativ's data analysis found.
The BGN voted on the final replacement names for 650 names in September 2022 and for 7 additional names in January 2023.
The Department of the Interior today announced the Board on Geographic Names (BGN) has voted on the final replacement names for nearly 650 geographic features featuring the word sq___.
On September 18, 2024 the U.S. Board on Geographic Names approved proposals to change the name of Negro Jack Creek in Tillamook County to Jack Creek
